text:
suresh: Heads up — 3 restore jobs this morning failed during KMS decrypt of snapshots after a cross-account copy. Getting AccessDenied from KMS.

suresh: Error snippet from restore-runner logs:
```
KMS:Decrypt error: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/restore-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:222:key/abc123

at com.redwood.restore.KMSClient.decrypt(KMSClient.java:87)
```

maryam: Do we create AWS Grants during the restore? Or are we relying on key policy/IAM only? :thinking_face:

alex: We normally create a transient grant from the CMK owner account to the restore role at restore-time. But for cross-account snapshot copies the grant creation is failing because the CMK policy/conditions were tightened in the last RBAC sweep.

rachel: I saw a change last week that removed `kms:CreateGrant` from the restore role in prod to harden RBAC. That might be the root cause. :lock:

suresh: Can we get a quick CloudTrail/Logs query to surface all recent `Decrypt`/`CreateGrant` failures?

maryam: CloudWatch Logs Insights that helped me:
```
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.arn, errorMessage
| filter eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com" and (eventName = "Decrypt" or eventName = "CreateGrant")
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 50
```

oncall: Copying this into the incident runbook. We should also create an alert for repeated `AccessDenied` on KMS keys used by backups. :bangbang:

encops-bot: Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-cross-account-restore (updated v2) :white_check_mark:

alex: Short-term options:
- Re-add `kms:CreateGrant` to the restore role with a strict condition (e.g. `aws:SourceAccount` == key-owner-account) and TTL-based grants.
- Or pivot to envelope re-encryption in the destination account (create a new data key under the destination CMK and re-encrypt snapshot objects) — more work but avoids cross-account grants.

maryam: Agreed. For immediate mitigation I propose a temporary key policy change on the CMK to explicitly allow `arn:aws:iam::111:role/restore-runner` `kms:Decrypt` for 2 hours, then roll back. That buys time to evaluate safer fixes.

rachel: I'll open a quick PR to revert the RBAC removal and add a scoped condition. Also adding CloudTrail metric filter for `kms:CreateGrant` failures and an alert. Creating JIRA INF-3421.

suresh: Long-term we should centralize grant handling in a single service account ("restore-service") that owns cross-account grants and has an audited workflow. Then restore runners assume that role instead of creating grants themselves.

alex: Also add tests in the restore CI to simulate copying snapshots to a different account and verify decrypt path (unit + integration).

maryam: For audit logging, add the following CloudTrail Insights rule to capture suspicious grant activity: `eventSource = "kms.amazonaws.com" and (eventName = "CreateGrant" or eventName = "RetireGrant" or eventName = "RevokeGrant")` and forward to the security log index.

suresh: Quick vuln triage note — we saw a weird failure pattern that matched an older `aws-sdk` bug where `CreateGrant` fails when the caller is an assumed role if the SDK version is old. We upgraded SDK in a few services last month; worth verifying the restore-runner's runtime.

oncall: Action items:
- rachel: PR to revert RBAC removal + add scoped condition (hotfix) — expected within 1h.
- maryam: prepare temp CMK policy that allows decrypt for 2h if PR not ready.
- alex: add CI test for cross-account restore (INF-3422).
- suresh: add CloudWatch/CloudTrail alert rule and add to oncall runbook.

rachel: Filing the PR now, adding `aws:SourceAccount` condition and a `kms:ViaService` guard. Will tag encops for review. :eyes:

maryam: After hotfix, we should schedule a follow-up to design the central restore-service and update the snapshot-copy docs. Also add a note in the backup runbook about required KMS grants/policies.

suresh: 👍 Thanks. If anyone sees additional AccessDenied spikes, ping `#eng-oncall` and I'll escalate.

encops-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-KMS-RESTORE (linked to INF-3421).
